ratio_definition: GPU wall time / CPU wall time; >1 means GPU slower

protocol.execution: All inference jobs serial; no CPU/GPU performance workloads overlapped. Each case in fresh process. No clock pinning; desktop system.
protocol.llama: Q8_0 language model and Q8_0 mmproj; n_gpu_layers=0 CPU or99 Vulkan; n_ctx_seq8192; n_parallel4; n_threads4 primary comparison; mmproj follows selected backend.
protocol.llama_primary_preload: LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libstdc++.so.6 on BOTH CPU and GPU. Installed wheel/source unchanged.
protocol.fixed_text: One warm-up + three timed; full prompt413 and forced128 output tokens each call; deterministic greedy; same content on both backends. Specialized OCR model produces repetitive text on this generic prompt: fixed-work throughput only, not answer-quality test.
protocol.six_image_ocr: Same six bundled PNGs as ONNX calibration; LLM preprocess differs from ONNX. Sequential single-image requests, natural EOS, max256 output tokens, one warm-up sweep + three timed sweeps. End-to-end request wall time includes image encoding/serialization and Python overhead. Every output exactly matches manifest text.
protocol.onnx: Actual batch[6,3,48,1012], CPU threads4/inter1, native WebGPU NHWC Vulkan. One process per graph/settings. Ten CPU runs then10 GPU runs; primary median discards first3. Every output finite and CTC tokens checked against CPU and previous runs. Stop on mismatch.
protocol.onnx_diagnostic: Architecture guard bypassed only in standalone diagnostic ORT script; production policy unchanged. CPU prepacking default; GPU no-prepack cases set session.disable_prepacking=1. GraphCapture off. No NCHW tests.
protocol.dml: Historical same-machine Windows measurements from2026-10-18, ORT1.24.4, original graph, 4/1threads, metacommands off, one warm-up + two timed sums,10 fresh workers. Linux cannot run DirectML natively; not rerun this session.

interpretation: Current UHD770 loses to CPU for both valid llama workloads and both valid ONNX comparisons.
Llama fixed-text ratio1.573 is close to historical DML1.606, but six-image Llama1.334 and diagnostic WebGPU2.238 differ. This is not evidence of a transferable numeric predictor.
Even within llama, prompt evaluation GPU/CPU0.768 and decode1.947 favor different devices. Document image sizes, output lengths and concurrency change the aggregate ratio.
WebGPU2.238 is a diagnostic raw-graph result after disabling prepacking; not a valid production compact-graph result or proof the full WebGPU pipeline is fixed.
DML versus WebGPU also differs in OS,ORT version,prepacking and protocol. The matching1+2 Linux diagnostic ratio2.194 still differs from DML1.606, but does not isolate execution-provider effects.

Use ONNX result as a prior or candidate-order hint; choose llama device with its own short representative vision/prefill/decode benchmark and output checks; cache by model,backend,device,driver and relevant thread/context settings.
On this machine prefer llama CPU based on valid measured workloads. Do not automatically extend the existing Linux WebGPU architecture rule to all Vulkan devices or other machines.
